Deputy Séamus McGrath  I understand the project has to be completed. That is not wasted money, in the sense that it has to happen. What is the element that will close out the wasted phase of this?
Mr. Paul Hendrick  I would say it is a few hundred grand per month, maximum for the next couple of months. Then, when we move to the final solution to deliver the project-----
Deputy Séamus McGrath  The €50 million is, therefore, going to grow.
Mr. Paul Hendrick  Yes, a bit, but it will stop, based on the decisions-----
Deputy Séamus McGrath  It could grow to €50.5 million.
Ms Mary Considine  The €50 million was an impairment figure written off on the balance sheet. There are ongoing current costs.
Deputy Séamus McGrath  My point is Irish Rail has not closed out this yet.
Ms Mary Considine  We have not.
Deputy Séamus McGrath  Therefore, there will be additional expenditure to close out the wasted phase of this. Irish Rail accepts that.
Ms Mary Considine  Yes.

Deputy Séamus McGrath  It is not in a position to say how much it will be, but it will be several hundred thousand euro.  The need for the TMS was identified and the contract was signed in 2020 to be delivered in 2024. It is not there. What is the current state of the TMS?

Ms Mary Considine  For the current TMS, we are using old technology. It is more than 20 years old and it will no longer be supported. That was the reason for moving to start this project in the first place but, in the interim period, once we knew the principles testing was not succeeding on the current version we had from Indra, we moved to look at a plan B around obsolescence to de-risk the greater Dublin area initially.
Deputy Séamus McGrath  Is the current system functional and safe?
Ms Mary Considine  The current system is safe. As I explained earlier, it is fail-safe. We will stop operations, but we will not compromise safety.
Deputy Séamus McGrath  What is Irish Rail stopping?
Ms Mary Considine  If there were a breakdown in the technology in the morning, it would have an impact on operations. We had a failure at the end of May.
Deputy Séamus McGrath  There are operational implications.
Ms Mary Considine  Yes, there are operational implications, but not safety implications.
Deputy Séamus McGrath  Service delivery will be impacted by a failure.
Ms Mary Considine  If we had not moved to de-risk the obsolescence risk, which we have now moved to do in the greater Dublin area. We need to look at a solution for the whole country.
Deputy Séamus McGrath  Where is Irish Rail in terms of replacing that system? It is trying to close out the Indra project. It needs a traffic management system. Where is it on delivering one?

Ms Mary Considine  All the decisions are interrelated so once we work through the next few weeks, we will engage with the NTA and the Department as our funders to secure funding for the way forward. We have a proposal to move forward.
Deputy Séamus McGrath  Does Irish Rail have an estimated cost for what it will take to get to a traffic management system that is modern and up-to-date?
Ms Mary Considine  We do, but for commercial reasons - we are in discussions - I cannot disclose that figure here.
Deputy Séamus McGrath  Can I have a ballpark figure?
Ms Mary Considine  Unfortunately, I cannot say, because I do not want to compromise-----
Deputy Séamus McGrath  Will it be tens of millions of euro?
Ms Mary Considine  It will be a significant figure but I cannot disclose it because we want to preserve commercial integrity.
Deputy Séamus McGrath  Will it be in the order of the €50 million writedown?
Ms Mary Considine  I am not in a position to say, unfortunately.
Deputy Séamus McGrath  It will be a significant sum.  Does Iarnród Éireann have a timeline for when it hopes to get an updated traffic management system?
Ms Mary Considine  We do. We are hopeful the obsolescence provisions can be addressed in 2027-28 and then we will move to complete the traffic management system by the end of the decade.

Deputy Séamus McGrath  We were due to have it by the end of 2024 but it will be 2030 at the earliest, from what Ms Considine said.  I will turn to the implications for budgets. With respect, Ms Considine kind of skirted around the implication for other projects earlier. This will have significant implications for other projects overseen by the NTA and Irish Rail. There is a €50 million writedown and to replace the TMS will cost an unknown amount but it will be a sizeable figure, as Ms Considine said. The money has to come from somewhere. Let us be honest about that. What will it have an impact on? Will the NTA address that point as the approving authority?

Ms Anne Shaw  We will have to look at it across the whole portfolio across the rail network to understand what is safety critical, what capacity is and so on and then work out what we will need to change in delivery timescales-----
Deputy Séamus McGrath  It is going to have implications for projects.

Ms Anne Shaw  The replacement of the traffic management system, as Ms Considine said, is a requirement so we have to make sure we can deliver it within the timeframe that has been set out. Then we will take that into consideration. Once we understand what that delivery is and its costs, we will need to do a review of the rest of the portfolio to be able to understand the impact.
Deputy Séamus McGrath  Ms Shaw mentioned the review that is costing almost €250,000. What is its aim?
Ms Anne Shaw  Is the Deputy talking about the EY review that has been commissioned by the NTA?
Deputy Séamus McGrath  Yes.

Ms Anne Shaw  It is to look back at the governance, decision-making and controls of the project from pre-procurement to where we find ourselves today. It will give us information about how the project was managed, how the governance was organised-----

Deputy Séamus McGrath  Respectfully, is there not enough ability within Iarnród Éireann and the NTA to sit down and figure out what went wrong here without bringing in a third party at a cost of €250,000, adding to the overall waste of public money? Is there not enough expertise within the organisations to pinpoint where things went wrong?

Ms Anne Shaw  As I mentioned in reply to a question earlier, it is always valuable to have an independent view, particularly so the organisations are not accused of not putting all the information into it.
Deputy Séamus McGrath  Are the terms of reference for the review such that there will ultimately be some accountability for what went wrong?
Ms Anne Shaw  There will be a series of findings and recommendations and both organisations will deliver against those recommendations, working with our colleagues in the Department of Transport.

Deputy Séamus McGrath  In this whole fiasco, it seems there is Iarnród Éireann, the NTA and the Department of Transport and everyone is responsible, but no one is responsible. Where does the accountability fall for this?

Ms Anne Shaw  There is accountability at different stages of the project. There is accountability in Iarnród Éireann for the delivery. There is accountability in the NTA for the approvals and oversight of the project and accountability in the Department for the overall programme.
Deputy Séamus McGrath  There is effectively no accountability. All parties here have said that it predates their time in office, so ultimately there will be no accountability for this.
Ms Anne Shaw  There are certainly people who will take responsibility and accountability for this project, particularly in moving this project forward.

Deputy Séamus McGrath  Finally, regarding the NTA, I have to say I have serious concerns about the organisation as a whole. We have constant correspondence between this committee and the NTA. We just have to look to the electric buses and the whole debacle over their storage, and the Busconnects project in Cork with €75 million spent on that alone and effectively very little to show for it. We have ongoing issues relating to bus reliability that have been highlighted for years now, and we seem to be making no progress with them.  The NTA is currently pumping out replies to anyone who asks about the delivery of new services that it does not have funding for it, and is pointing the finger to the Department of Transport, yet we are here today discussing a monumental waste of public money. There are serious governance and management issues with the NTA that have to be addressed.  Would the witnesses like to comment on that?

Ms Anne Shaw  I take the points the Deputy has raised quite seriously. However, there has been an element of delivery across the projects to move them forward within the project life cycle. We have continued to work through decisions around the capital programme and with the Department of Transport in planning for new services as part of Busconnects. There is always expenditure before you do the infrastructure delivery, etc., to make sure we are delivering the right thing, but those projects are moving forward and will deliver benefits for this country in terms of sustainable public transport access.
Deputy Séamus McGrath  Thank you.

Mr. Tomás Campbell  Briefly, on the PSO point, for the PSO budget this year we got a 43% uplift from the Department of public expenditure, which puts us at a much better baseline in 2027. In the NTA's defence, part of the budget setting was that there would not be new services this year and it would be a year of consolidation. The Minister, Deputy O'Brien, has been clear on that as well.  In the past, we have rolled out new services, particularly with driver availability and the availability of electric buses, which the Deputy mentioned, but this year is about catching up. As part of the budget negotiations in October for 2027, we will be advocating for additional funding for additional services next year, but this year has been to try to consolidate the services.
Deputy James Geoghegan  I thank all the witnesses for being here today. Am I right in saying the original project budget for the national train control centre was €148 million?
Ms Anne Shaw  Yes.
Deputy James Geoghegan  In the NTA 2024 accounts, it was estimated the project cost had increased to €189 million, which constituted a 28% cost overrun. Is that correct?
Ms Anne Shaw  Yes, that is correct.

Deputy James Geoghegan  In the document the witnesses have supplied for us today, it states, "indicating an optimistic best case of forecast outturn cost." They are now saying it is going to cost €250 million, which would represent a 70% increase on the original budget. What does the NTA attribute that cost increase to?

Mr. Hugh Creegan  That comment in the briefing note is a briefing given to the Irish Rail board. That figure of €250 million is not settled yet. As it was mentioned earlier, we still have to work through what the next stage of the project is. We will then have a firm figure, but we do not have that yet.
Deputy James Geoghegan  What is the provenance of that €250 million figure?

Ms Mary Considine  As I said to Deputy McGrath earlier, we are considering all these and, in a matter of weeks, we hope to have more certainty. However, I cannot confirm the figure at this stage. I think that figure was a rough order of magnitude.

Deputy James Geoghegan  Hold on. The witnesses supplied documents to this committee and told us it was €250 million. I have a very simple question: what is the provenance of that €250 million figure, which is €60 million more than the figure given to us at the end of 2024? Can Ms Considine even explain that €60 million increase?

Ms Mary Considine  I understand the reference to the €250 million figure was an outer range, if the project was to continue over the next number of years. It is not a figure that relates to where we are today and what would be required.
Deputy James Geoghegan  How did the NTA get to that figure?
Ms Mary Considine  I might hand that over to Mr. Hendrick.

Mr. Paul Hendrick  In reference to the €189 million figure, we put forward a range a few years ago when we were working through the project with Indra and were expecting to complete the project with Indra, but obviously later than planned. Commercial reset number two put us into the 2027 completion timeline and we did a risk assessment against how late it may be against that.  We did a project range forecast of €175 million to €205 million, which is where the €189 million comes from; it is the midpoint.
Deputy James Geoghegan  Can Mr. Hendrick tell me how we are now at €250 million?

Mr. Paul Hendrick  The source of this goes back to the lack of a developed product from Indra, which is driving the project delays. That €250 million, which is in our briefing note, is an indicative estimate. It is just extrapolating based on time. It is the time delay to complete the project and the level of resource effort that would likely be required to complete the project. That is what it is driven by.
Deputy James Geoghegan  As for the resource effort Mr. Hendrick is talking about there, is that buying a new TMS software project from a new supplier? The NTA estimates that will cost €60 million.
Mr. Paul Hendrick  That is provisional because we have not got to the final decision on the way forward.
Ms Mary Considine  Basically, that was based on Indra continuing over an elongated period.

Deputy James Geoghegan  The witnesses are both saying completely contradictory things. One is saying that relates to the acquisition of new software, while the other is saying it relates to Indra. Which is it?

Mr. Paul Hendrick  The briefing document, as it was done at the time, was on the basis that if we stayed going with Indra, albeit without any predictability of where it was going to finish, it could end up in that particular zone or territory. We have not finalised that way forward yet, so we cannot-----
Deputy James Geoghegan  I just asked Mr. Hendrick a moment ago if that related to the acquisition of a new TMS software, and he said "Yes". He nodded as I was speaking to him.

Mr. Paul Hendrick  Either way, we are going to have expenditure more than the €205 million we indicated in that range, whatever way we go forward with the project, because the project is going to finish significantly beyond 2027.
Deputy James Geoghegan  I said that is €60 million more, and that figure the NTA has talked about is for the new software it is potentially going to have to acquire-----
Mr. Paul Hendrick  There will be costs to that new software.
Deputy James Geoghegan  The NTA has estimated that at €60 million.
Mr. Paul Hendrick  No, we do not have a final figure for that.
Deputy James Geoghegan  I did not say the witnesses had that final figure. I said the figure the witnesses have given us, and by the way, I am only questioning figures they have given us-----
Mr. Paul Hendrick  Yes, exactly.
Deputy James Geoghegan  That is all I am doing.
Mr. Paul Hendrick  That figure relates to Indra.
Deputy James Geoghegan  It does not relate to any future costs the NTA would need to acquire new software.
Mr. Paul Hendrick  It does not, because we have not got to the final decision or solution there. We still need to finalise what that will be and those figures, so that figure does not relate to it.
Deputy James Geoghegan  What is the point of the €250 million figure? What is the NTA trying to tell us?

Mr. Paul Hendrick  If the project continued with Indra, albeit with no definitive timeline. We did an estimate for the board at that time, when we put that into the document, of where this could end up if the project continued with Indra beyond 2030.
Deputy James Geoghegan  If the project continues to not deliver the software the NTA needs.
Mr. Paul Hendrick  If the project continued to deliver and was completed as per originally planned, albeit much later.
Deputy James Geoghegan  It would go to €250 million.
Mr. Paul Hendrick  It could.
Deputy James Geoghegan  If the contract with Indra is terminated, what do the witnesses think the cost will be?
Mr. Paul Hendrick  We cannot say the definite number at this time because we have not got the final decision agreed on how we would move forward with that. We will have to finalise that figure.

Deputy James Geoghegan  According to The Irish Times and the letter Irish Rail sent to the NTA, the plan is to look for an exception outside the normal rules of public procurement and get Siemens Mobility to provide the TMS service. That is what was reported in The Irish Times . That is Irish Rail's plan but it needs approval, is that correct?
Mr. Paul Hendrick  I do not think we can go into that. It goes back to-----

Ms Mary Considine  It is unfortunate that things are covered outside of process, but we have to follow the process and preserve the legal and commercial integrity of the discussions that are currently-----
Deputy James Geoghegan  It is the NTA's plan to look outside of public procurement to replace the software, is that not correct?

Ms Mary Considine  At present, we have proven in-use technology on our network that is capable and is part of our strategy to de-risk the obsolescence risk in this area, which is an option going forward. However, we cannot prejudge what will happen over the coming weeks.

Deputy James Geoghegan  Obviously, if you issue a notice, that is a public notice and will be published on eTenders or whatever, if Irish Rail is looking to go outside the public procurement rules. Mr. Hendrick mentioned earlier he was advocating that, in certain circumstances, going outside the tender rules could be a better outcome for the delivery of software. This was reported in The Irish Times with reference to the letter. We are sort of dancing around a pin here. That is the plan. Whatever about Siemens - maybe the witnesses cannot talk about that - the plan is to go outside public procurement to replace the software. The witnesses can say that, can they not?
Mr. Paul Hendrick  I do not think it is strictly correct to say it is outside of public procurement, per se .

Deputy James Geoghegan  Sorry, the witnesses are looking for a lawful exception to go outside the standard. The NTA is not going to issue a tender; it is going to directly engage. It is going to do it in a different way through the existing public procurement rules.

Mr. Paul Hendrick  We are looking at different routes and avenues to it, but I have to go back to the comment from my colleague earlier about the whole thing.  We are still in contract with Indra-----

Deputy James Geoghegan  Going back to the original contract, is Mr. Hendrick familiar with the term "abnormally low pricing bid"? He indicated that the bid was 50% lower than the other bid that Indra was-----
Mr. Paul Hendrick  If I may just correct myself, because I misspoke earlier, the unsuccessful tender was 50% higher. Technically, it is just to do with the percentage-----
Deputy James Geoghegan  That is okay, but it was a very big differential.
Mr. Paul Hendrick  There was a differential between them.
Deputy James Geoghegan  An enormous differential.
Mr. Paul Hendrick  Sizeable, yes.
Deputy James Geoghegan  Well, it is not prescribed but, typically, as I understand it, an abnormally low bid would be between 15% and 20%, but Mr. Hendrick said it was 50%.

Mr. Paul Hendrick  If I may just say this, because I have to be careful around the commercial sensitivities of that information as well, we have the NEC contract model, so we were able to have full insight into how those prices were made up in a way you might not see in other contract models. The differential was driven by the fee approaches that the bidders took. One bidder had a similar cost base, if that makes sense, but how they marked up their cost to generate their price was very different from the successful tender-----
Deputy James Geoghegan  Nevertheless, it was 50% more.
Mr. Paul Hendrick  As a total, it was of that order.
Deputy James Geoghegan  Mr. Hendrick knows the legal obligations that apply to contracting authorities when an abnormally low tender bid happens. Was an investigation carried out at the time?

Mr. Paul Hendrick  It was investigated. It was assessed. We do a normalisation process to work through that. Based on the visibility of the prime cost of the work for both bidders, they were both in a similar range, but it was the fee differential that was different. We worked through a process to satisfy ourselves that it did not meet the legal standard for abnormally low. That was the procurement decision that was reached and that led to the contract award.

Deputy James Geoghegan  In respect of the issue Mr. Hendrick raised about the two versions of the software, he said that Iarnród Éireann had examined it and that, legally, Indra was not in breach of contract. Obviously, Iarnród Éireann sought or relied on legal advice in the context of examining this issue.

Mr. Paul Hendrick  I was not in this position at the time but, in terms of my understanding of what the project team went through, we assessed it with the project team, the engineering professionals on the project and the people who were working to manage the contract. I cannot say whether there was legal advice taken on that particular decision. I would have to come back to the Deputy on it.
Deputy James Geoghegan  But Mr. Hendrick indicated earlier that, legally, it was not a breach of contract.
Mr. Paul Hendrick  There are project professionals. Some of them are not lawyers, but they are-----
Deputy James Geoghegan  Mr. Hendrick does not know yet whether Iarnród Éireann has assessed whether that constitutes a legal breach of contract.

Mr. Paul Hendrick  The assessment decision was made by the project team at the time, including by people who are there to professionally manage the contract, not necessarily lawyers. We do not have lawyers working in project delivery, let us say, but they are still responsible for managing the contract, managing claims, deciding whether a claim has entitlement or not, establishing whether there is a breach of contract. This is normal with all our projects. In certain cases, depending on the situation, we also take legal advice. I cannot say whether-----

Deputy James Geoghegan  My time is short, so I will ask just one final question. The restart agreement was a sort of contract agreement at the end of 2024 between Iarnród Éireann and Indra based on all the deliberations, is that correct? Iarnród Éireann agreed to the restart agreement and six months later identified problems. Going forward, is Mr. Hendrick concerned that Iarnród Éireann has sort of lost its right to moan about everything that went wrong before the restart agreement in the context of any future recourse it may wish to take? Is that going to prove problematic for it as the contracting authority?
Mr. Paul Hendrick  I go back to a comment from my colleague earlier. We are still in contract with Indra. This is all commercially and legally sensitive, so it is difficult for me to-----

Deputy James Geoghegan  During this hearing and in the documents he has provided, however, Mr. Hendrick has identified several moments when challenges, concerns and red flags arose. He has put all that out there. Once Iarnród Éireann executed a new agreement with Indra, is Mr. Hendrick concerned that it might be problematic into the future in terms of any recourse Iarnród Éireann might have against Indra?
Mr. Paul Hendrick  It depends.

An Cathaoirleach  I thank Deputy Geoghegan. I will ask some questions. Six years after the initial contract and two years after the full implementation of the TMS was due to be delivered, how much has actually been delivered? We know it was broken up into different CPs. CP1, for example, represented what percentage of the entirety of the contract?
Mr. Paul Hendrick  CP1, which was the Rosslare line, was about 3% of the overall-----
An Cathaoirleach  About 3%.
Mr. Paul Hendrick  Yes. It is about 6% of-----

An Cathaoirleach  In terms of complexity, that was the easier part to implement. We are talking about a write-down of €50 million, which is growing, and other costs, which I will get into in a moment, and we have not even seen 3% delivered.
Mr. Paul Hendrick  That is correct.

An Cathaoirleach  We talk about red flags and interventions. That speaks volumes. As regards the contract with Indra, Ms Considine stated that the company has embarked on a legal process. Has Indra been informed legally that the contract is going to be terminated?
Ms Mary Considine  As stated earlier, we really cannot go into that. We are still in contract with Indra and-----
An Cathaoirleach  We are dancing on the head of a pin here. A decision was taken by the board-----
Ms Mary Considine  Decisions have been taken and-----
An Cathaoirleach  -----of Irish Rail, supported by the NTA, and we cannot say what was involved.
Ms Mary Considine  We would have confirmation of the support of the NTA on Monday afternoon, so we need to work through that. The Cathaoirleach will appreciate that it is only Thursday.
An Cathaoirleach  Has ministerial consent been asked for or is ministerial consent needed?

Mr. Tomás Campbell  At this point, no. Ms Considine mentioned the resilience measures. Because of the delays relating to the traffic management system, which had two parts, which were to deliver a traffic management system for the country-----
An Cathaoirleach  Has the Minister given approval to terminate the contract?
Mr. Tomás Campbell  No. Ministerial approval would not be required, but the Minister has approved resilience works through the infrastructure-----

An Cathaoirleach  I will get to that in a minute. I want to talk about the decision to seek a capital investments lead on the project. Whose decision was it that capital investments in Irish Rail would lead out on this?
Mr. Paul Hendrick  It would have been the CEO at the time.

An Cathaoirleach  In light of your experience in capital investments, you might give us some examples of IT projects that capital investments delivered successfully in the years prior to the decision to enter this contract.
Mr. Paul Hendrick  Capital investments is primarily delivering all the new railway infrastructure projects and rolling stock projects-----
An Cathaoirleach  Physical infrastructure, engineering projects-----
Mr. Paul Hendrick  -----and that includes signalling. I want to make this distinction, because it is really important. The train control system is a signalling project. It involves-----
An Cathaoirleach  What IT experience existed in capital investments?

Mr. Paul Hendrick  May I just say, it involves hardware and software. We are dealing with hardware and software and other signalling projects, which we are delivering to plan. This is not an IT project. I appreciate that it has the hallmarks of one because of what it has become, but it is a signalling project - a signalling system. Because of the difficulties-----
An Cathaoirleach  A signalling project that heavily depended on IT and technology.
Mr. Paul Hendrick  There is hardware and software in every signalling project, but you should not have an IT-type project delivery when you have a developed signalling product-----
An Cathaoirleach  What specific IT experience-----
Mr. Paul Hendrick  Capital investments are not an IT delivery organisation, and we were not delivering IT projects. I want to make that clear.
An Cathaoirleach  Who would be the person within Irish Rail who would have the competent head of technology?
Ms Mary Considine  Technology sits in a number of areas. There-----
An Cathaoirleach  Who is the competent head?
Ms Mary Considine  We have a chief information officer, CIO, for the organisation who would look after all the infrastructure.
An Cathaoirleach  What role did the CIO play?
Ms Mary Considine  He would have sat on the initial project board. I can confirm that afterwards. We also have operational technology that, as my colleague Mr. Hendrick said-----

An Cathaoirleach  The information I have is that the competent head was never involved in the project from the very start right through to design to tender to project management, or, indeed, in the intervening years. You might come back to us-----
Ms Mary Considine  I will come back and clarify. That is fine.
An Cathaoirleach  -----if you want to contradict that. It has been reported that payment to Indra stopped in April?
Mr. Paul Hendrick  It was February.
An Cathaoirleach  February. There is a claim by Indra. A figure of €5.67 million has been put out there. What is the timeframe relating to that claim.

Mr. Paul Hendrick  Indra has raised a number of claims relating to the period 2025 to 2026. We have assessed the claims that have been submitted and they have been rejected as lacking entitlement under the contract.
An Cathaoirleach  All claims have been rejected.
Mr. Paul Hendrick  They have been professionally assessed. We have assessed them thoroughly against the contract and we have rejected them.
An Cathaoirleach  There is no outstanding claim for €5.67 million.

Mr. Paul Hendrick  There is a claim there. We have rejected it but Indra has not rejected our rejection of its claim thus far. I am not saying it will not reject our rejection. If it wants to do so, it is entitled to under the contract. All I am saying is that it has not done that yet.

An Cathaoirleach  On the cost, we know there was a write-down of €50 million. The witnesses have touched on the existing train management system in Connolly Station. Over €6 million in funding has been allocated. Is that to strengthen the system or what is it to do?
Ms Mary Considine  That funding was made available through the Department of Transport to allow us to address the obsolescence issues.
An Cathaoirleach  How much funding was provided?
Ms Mary Considine  It is in and around the figure the Cathaoirleach mentioned for this year.
An Cathaoirleach  It is €6 million for this year. What is it for next year?
Ms Mary Considine  I cannot give a figure for next year.
Mr. Tomás Campbell  Iarnród Éireann submitted a proposal to us for about €20 million over three years for that work.
An Cathaoirleach  That is €20 million over three years.

Mr. Tomás Campbell  It proposed €20 million over the next three years but we have only given approval for the first year of the project. While we recognise the importance of the resilience works, we did not want to pre-empt the software testing phase with Indra and any subsequent decisions around the TMS more generally. At this point-----
An Cathaoirleach  This €20 million is to shore up a 20-year-old system that is outdated-----
Mr. Tomás Campbell  No.
Ms Mary Considine  No.
An Cathaoirleach  -----and that was due to be replaced.
Mr. Tomás Campbell  It is not. It is to deliver a new system that will-----
An Cathaoirleach  It is for a completely new system.

Mr. Tomás Campbell  -----work in parallel with the old system. The benefit of that is that it gives us greater redundancy in signalling in the greater Dublin area. It will support the direction of the DART+ programme. It also frees up some spare parts from the older obsolete system at Connolly Station so it gives us more resilience across the entire network. That system is no longer supported and we are running out of spare parts. Over the next three years, we will see a signalling solution in Dublin and greater resilience across the entirety of the network.

An Cathaoirleach  There are further concerns in relation to a new signalling system in Cork that is due to come into being in August 2027. According to the minutes provided by Irish Rail, if there is a delay to the commissioning date for the Cork signalling system, it could lead to additional costs on the project, including contractor delay claims and internal and external project management claims of up to €800,000 per month. That system depends on a train management system being in place to underpin it. Will the witnesses give us some reassurance? The necessary TMS was to be the system Indra was going to deliver, which is now clearly not going to happen. What reassurance can the witnesses give us that a system will be in place to ensure there are no financial penalties in relation to that particular signalling system?

Ms Mary Considine  Part of resolving where we are at the moment and moving forward is looking at how we can deliver a train control system for the entire country. As Mr. Campbell has said, with the benefit of funding from the Department, we are able to address the greater Dublin area. We now need to look at a solution for the whole country. The Cork area commuter rail project is a critical project. We do not want to have to delay or implicate that.
An Cathaoirleach  We have just over 12 months.
Ms Mary Considine  We are looking at options.

An Cathaoirleach  We have just over 12 months. Can you give us assurance that a system will be in place to underpin that new signalling system, which is due to commence in August 2027, to ensure no financial penalties are imposed?
Ms Mary Considine  That will be a key consideration of ours. We will obviously be putting forward a case for funding to secure that.

An Cathaoirleach  There is no funding and no one in place to deliver that. Am I right in saying there are penalties of up to €800,000 written into that contract in addition to other financial considerations? We are facing serious financial repercussions if we do not have a system in place by August 2027.
Ms Mary Considine  The Cathaoirleach is right that there will be costs if we do not come up with a solution but, as he has said, there are 12-----
An Cathaoirleach  There will be costs to the tune of €800,000 a month.

Ms Mary Considine  That was an estimated cost. The key thing here is that, as you have rightly said, we are 12 months away. There are options and we need to make sure they are put in place to avoid that cost.
An Cathaoirleach  Are you confident we will avoid that cost?
Ms Mary Considine  We will do everything we can to-----
An Cathaoirleach  There is no confidence there.
Ms Mary Considine  I cannot guarantee the funding but that is certainly our intention.

An Cathaoirleach  We have written off €50 million. That is wasted. Some €20 million is being provided for a system for the greater Dublin area, which is only necessary because of the failure to deliver the TMS. There are further financial considerations next year because of this failure. The millions are ratcheting up here constantly. That is before we actually move towards putting in place a TMS.

Ms Mary Considine  To clarify, that is a TMS. The work we are doing in the greater Dublin area is a traffic control system. If we come up with a solution for Cork, it will be a permanent solution. This is not wasted money. It is the solution.

An Cathaoirleach  I want to talk about the rest of the country outside the GDA. One of my colleagues touched on potentially giving a contract directly to Siemens. I believe Siemens withdrew from the initial tendering process. I would have concerns about bypassing normal procurement rules. Anyone looking to deliver a train management system has the State over a barrel. I would have serious concerns that anyone looking to deliver such a system could just name their price. I might ask the Comptroller and Auditor General's office for a view on concerns relating to bypassing a normal procurement process and awarding a contract of such a nature directly.

Ms Colette Drinan  I am obviously not going to comment on Iarnród Éireann and its operations specifically. In procurement, openness, transparency and competition are needed to underpin value for money. That is the standard. In exceptional circumstances, stepping away from that can be justified but a very clear audit trail would be necessary. It is a complex matter. There would be a need for legal advice and so on to underpin it.

An Cathaoirleach  I would have serious concerns that any prospective deliverer of a TMS will have the State over a barrel because of the situation Irish Rail finds itself in. I will touch on another couple of areas quickly. Have people been recruited to work in the national control centre? How many staff does Irish Rail currently employ in that centre?

Mr. Paul Hendrick  We have a number of operations. We control a number of aspects of the railway from the national control centre. These include control of the overhead powerlines for the DART network, some of the CCTV systems, level crossings and a part of the network on the Sligo line. That is as was always planned. That has been delivered because it was not dependent on the Indra project. There are a number of staff in there. We would have to come back to the Cathaoirleach with the number. It is low because it is not the full complement.

An Cathaoirleach  I have seen some of the recruitment advertising. The figure I have been given is that up to 30 staff have been recruited over the last two years to work on the signalling system and the TMS. Were any people employed specifically to be trained to operate the TMS?
Mr. Paul Hendrick  We would have employed some people in preparation for CP1 going live.
An Cathaoirleach  How many?
Mr. Paul Hendrick  I would have to come back to the Cathaoirleach. I do not have the number to hand.
An Cathaoirleach  Are they still in employment?
Mr. Paul Hendrick  Yes, my understanding is that whoever we have employed-----
An Cathaoirleach  There are people sitting in the national control centre twiddling their thumbs and waiting for Indra to deliver CP1.

Mr. Paul Hendrick  No. They are controlling what can be controlled from the NTCC building at the moment based on the assets that are being managed from the building today. We have obviously scaled back recruitment. Until we have certainty on the programme, we need to look at staff-----
An Cathaoirleach  Could that figure be up to 30 staff?
Mr. Paul Hendrick  Is the Cathaoirleach asking about all the staff who are in there today across 24-7 operations?
An Cathaoirleach  I am asking about staff working on that kind of-----

Mr. Paul Hendrick  It could be but I would have to come back to you on it. There would not be 30 on any given shift. There would be a smaller number on a standard shift. We would have to come back to you.

Ms Mary Considine  To clarify, a number of the control desks have migrated in there, as Mr. Hendrick was saying. There are staff working on those desks on a 24-7 basis. They are using the existing technology, however.
An Cathaoirleach  There has been a considerable cost. Some of these staff would have been trained up on the TMS and CP1.

Mr. Paul Hendrick  That is limited. We had to scale that back given the programme difficulties with Indra. We only have the staff there to manage what is currently being managed and controlled from the control room.

An Cathaoirleach  You might come back to us with more information on the costs associated with that. We will go back to the members. With the agreement of the witnesses, we will open it up for a second round of five minutes per speaker.

Deputy Grace Boland  The drip feed of information we have received about this project is not acceptable. It is essential that we get clear and transparent information from the NTA, Irish Rail and the Department on this and all other projects.  When we look at the governance structure of this project, it was more complicated than a small multinational, yet the only entity in this whole fiasco that seems to have been raising red flag, particularly since 2020 and seriously from 2022, was the sponsoring authority. Why did the NTA not step in earlier and resolve this issue? Why did the Department not step in earlier? It is simply not good enough.

Mr. Hugh Creegan  The NTA has been actively involved over the past four years as the problem arose. It was not the case of us being blind to it. At various points along the problem cycle, we made joint decisions with Irish Rail as to what should happen and that has been the case for the past two years. It has not been the case that we have been blind to it.

Deputy Grace Boland  Reading between the lines and reading Irish Rail's submissions and the numerous times it raised issues with the NTA, it was screaming, "Help, get us out of this; help, we need to terminate this", at the NTA. The decision - the joint decision apparently - always seemed to continue, that we would throw millions more at this project. What does that say about the NTA's oversight?

Mr. Hugh Creegan  At each point, we had a particular issue to deal with. We did grapple with the choices and, as the Deputy can see, impairment and all the consequences are really big issues. With Irish Rail, we looked at the alternatives. There was a major meeting with Indra in 2024 where we demanded an immediate plan to remedy the project. We did get a plan off it that seemed credible and we proceeded with that. Ultimately, it did not deliver. Last year, a report from WSP identified something that could deliver this but it would need to be done in a different way with a series of recommendations. Together with Irish Rail, we sought to do exactly that so at each point along the project, we have tried to rescue it.

Deputy Grace Boland  That is the point. It was clear to me a year ago, and I was not even in the weeds of it a year ago, that this project was failing when I started questions about it. The NTA was in the weeds of it so it should have been clearer to it much earlier.  I want to move on because we have not even reached the buses. Is the NTA acquiring buses? Is it the approving authority or the sponsoring authority or both? I am so confused by the various different blurred lines of the far too many hats worn by the NTA.
Mr. Hugh Creegan  When it comes to buses, it is crystal clear. We purchase the buses.
Deputy Grace Boland  Which means it is the sponsoring authority. Who is the NTA's oversight authority?
Mr. Hugh Creegan  In the case of BusConnects, we set an internal programme board with-----
Deputy Grace Boland  Who does it report to? The NTA probably.
Mr. Hugh Creegan  No, we have external members and our board is chaired by an external person. That board acts as the approving authority for certain decisions of the project.
Deputy Grace Boland  Who does that board report to?
Mr. Hugh Creegan  Ultimately, we all report to the Department of Transport.

Deputy Grace Boland  We need to get back into that again in September. In terms of the position the Department and the NTA seem to be taking on the buses, that we are saving money by having buses sitting in storage, as has been said in the Dáil and the documents provided here today, we need to see a very detailed cost-benefit analysis of how the Department is coming to that conclusion. It leads me to believe that the indexation of the inflation clauses in the framework agreement are far too generous. This needs to be looked at by the Department.  In terms of the planning, I refute the contention by the NTA that you cannot plan the planning phase of the delivery of the electric grid charger at the same time as ordering buses. It should not be a case of one after the other, which seems to be what the NTA is saying it should be. The NTA should know how long it is going to take in each local authority for it to obtain the planning permission and then order the buses based on that. It is not rocket science. Some of the stuff in here such as contending that we would have had to delay it until the infrastructure was in place is simply unacceptable if there was any project management capability on this.
Mr. Tomás Campbell  I will come briefly.
Deputy Grace Boland  Mr. Campbell is very brave. Mr. Creegan was about to come in there. Let us hear from Mr. Creegan.

Mr. Tomás Campbell  Regarding the analysis of the storage costs versus the bus one year later, inflation clauses probably may have been standard at the time but that period was the time of the Ukraine war so inflation probably was quite high. That analysis has been done by the NTA and does stack up.
Deputy Grace Boland  We have not seen it. All we have seen is this rhetoric. The Committee of Public Accounts has not seen the detail. Do not tell us it is saving us money without showing us.
Mr. Tomás Campbell  It is costing money but it is costing less as-----
Deputy Grace Boland  It certainly is.

Mr. Tomás Campbell  Mr. Creegan will come back in more detail on this. We have had a century of internal combustion engine buses. They are easy to install. It is a case of build a depot and drive them in. We are doing all of this for the first time. Research and development, getting planning applications in and get planning approval are happening for the first time. All of that has happened for the first time and there have been problems but the NTA has installed-----
Deputy Grace Boland  It is not rocket science.
Mr. Hugh Creegan  We did exactly what the Deputy suggested. We tried to align the provision of chargers and the purchase of buses.
Deputy Grace Boland  There were two failed procurement processes. That is a serious reflection on the NTA - two failed procurement processes for electricity-charging infrastructure.
Mr. Hugh Creegan  We can buy the buses, but when it comes to putting the chargers in the depots, the depots are run by the bus operators so they ran those procurement competitions.
Deputy Grace Boland  It is always someone else.

Mr. Hugh Creegan  They are the facts. We did align the bus purchasing programme and the charger installation programme, so at the start of the process, they were aligned. Due to problems that arose, they became disconnected and we ended up with the problems we have.
Deputy Joe Neville  I want to bring it back to a really high level. In some ways, I know the answer but what exact amount has been spent on the project to date? Is it €150 million?
Ms Mary Considine  It is €150 million plus €3 million to date this year.
Deputy Joe Neville  Could Ms Considine clarify the figure of €3 million?
Ms Mary Considine  The figure of €3 million is the ongoing cost of managing the project this year.
Deputy Joe Neville  Who is getting that money?

Ms Mary Considine  As Mr. Hendrick would have said, we have stopped paying Indra since February so there would be some Indra costs in there and then there would be third-party costs and our own project management costs.
Deputy Joe Neville  Is Irish Rail continuing to capitalise that?
Ms Mary Considine  No.
Deputy Joe Neville  So that is going through Irish Rail's current expenditure. Does that affect its current budget? Is it something Irish Rail had assumed would be in the costs in its budget?
Mr. Paul Hendrick  We would have seen it-----
(Interruptions).
Mr. Paul Hendrick  -----when we set that budget last year.
Deputy Joe Neville  So it will affect Irish Rail's current budget. That is money it would not have budgeted for. If it is not capitalising it now-----
Mr. Paul Hendrick  It is coming out of the capital side, which is going through profit and loss, but it was meant to go into the balance sheet.
Deputy Joe Neville  I know, but it is actually going through profit and loss. It is an expense. Irish Rail would not have put it in.
Ms Mary Considine  It is, but it is in and out because of funding.

Deputy Joe Neville  I am very conscious that Ms Considine is new to her role. Was this something she quickly saw as a red flag when she assumed her role? I am conscious that she has come in. It was written off in her time. How long has she been in her role.
Ms Mary Considine  I am about nine months in.
Deputy Joe Neville  So essentially she is trying to clear the decks.
Ms Mary Considine  My first board meeting was in October when there was a red flag in respect of this. We really focused-----
Deputy Joe Neville  Was it highlighted at the meeting?

Ms Mary Considine  It would have been flagged as a red flag project in the first board reporting. We are managing a significant portfolio of projects - €3.6 billion in phase six execution - and this was the one with the red flag on it.

Deputy Joe Neville  Can someone tell me what the old CEO thought of this, because we know Ms Considine cleared the decks? All too often, we come in after hearing that the person who had previous oversight has gone. Does anyone know what his stated view was?
Ms Mary Considine  I cannot speak for anyone else but if the Deputy looks-----
Deputy Joe Neville  On the record.
Ms Mary Considine  -----at all the data, concerns were raised all the way through and there would have been a number of senior meetings with Indra to try to resolve this.
Deputy Joe Neville  Did he ever wish for it to be written off? It is just interesting that Ms Considine came in and wrote it off straight away. What was his view?
Ms Mary Considine  As we discussed earlier, there was no discussion at the board about impairment because it was still working on a way forward.
Deputy Joe Neville  That was despite the fact that there were a serious amount of flags.
Ms Mary Considine  There were serious flags but as my colleague has said there were two commercial rebasings of it on the basis that everybody believed the project was going to be delivered.
Deputy Joe Neville  With the €152 million capitalised; I am sorry, how much is capitalised on the books now?
Ms Mary Considine  There is €100 million of-----
Deputy Joe Neville  There is €100 million capitalised, €53 million written off of a current total expense of-----
Ms Mary Considine  Yes.

Deputy Joe Neville  Okay. Where are we with the project? What if I am asked today? Someone says we have wasted €50 million and asks me where we are with the other €100 million. From a holistic perspective-----
Ms Mary Considine  The €100 million is a building in use. We have-----
Deputy Joe Neville  It is a building in use.
Ms Mary Considine  It is in use. As we spoke of earlier on, a number of our controllers our working out there based on existing technology.
Deputy Joe Neville  Are we happy with the build-up of that cost basis? I mean the capitalised nature of it.
Ms Mary Considine  Yes.
Mr. Paul Hendrick  No write-down on the building.

Deputy Joe Neville  That is what I am saying. The officials are happy that the €50 million is not linked to the €100 million, so it is just the software cost of the same project. What is the building being used for?

Ms Mary Considine  The building is being used by our own team who are operating on existing technology we plan to replace. Gardaí are also operating out of there and the building has been future-proofed for Dublin City Council.
Deputy Joe Neville  Dublin City Council.
Ms Mary Considine  Yes, to look to control the overall traffic system for the city.
Deputy Joe Neville  Okay, so we have a €100 million building but all the software - essentially, the actual project - is gone.
Ms Mary Considine  Just on the €100 million, you have the building, hardware costs for the new technology-----
Deputy Joe Neville  I am conscious of-----
Ms Mary Considine  -----and a lot of enabling work was done around the network for the new train control system.
Deputy Joe Neville  How much do we believe will have to be spent? I assume this project will have to go ahead in some shape or form. What is the cost going to be of that project?
Ms Mary Considine  I am just repeating myself, and I apologise, but it is at a sensitive time commercially and legally, so I cannot answer that.
Deputy Joe Neville  But we are going to go down that route again.
Ms Mary Considine  I am happy to come back and clarify once we are through the-----
Deputy Joe Neville  I know, but the project still has to be done.
Ms Mary Considine  Absolutely.

Deputy Joe Neville  That is fine.  This is more maybe for the NTA. What are the ramifications for it? We have a lot of projects coming up like DART+ West, DART+ South West and MetroLink. How do we feel? This involves the Department of public expenditure as well. At the infrastructure committee we had the interim CEO of MetroLink in. At the budgetary oversight committee, the Department of public expenditure was saying it does not really have a role because that role is subbed out to other people. The Department was not aware of this issue when I raised it on Tuesday. It seems strange to me that people at senior levels in that Department are not necessarily aware of a €50 million write-off in an entity where ultimately it is writing the cheques. I am not asking where the learnings are going to be because I hate asking that question, but what are the implications and ramifications considering the significant amount of money we are going to have to spend on infrastructure to bring it up if we can miss out on a project like this which showed many red flags? Was it 63 tests I saw were failed along the way, or where issues were brought up?
Ms Mary Considine  There were over 600 test log issues with 63 kind of substantial issues, I believe.

Deputy Joe Neville  There were 63 flagged failures on a project over many years, yet we just come to the end and someone new comes in and says we need to write that off because ultimately we have nothing to show for it.

Mr. Tomás Campbell  I will come in first from the Department's perspective. To take the point on the Department of public expenditure, we have been engaging with our Transport Vote colleagues in the Department, so they are aware of these issues. We have been-----
Deputy Joe Neville  The senior levels of the Department of public expenditure were not.
Mr. Tomás Campbell  That would be at principal officer level. I am not sure internally then how it was communicated-----
Deputy Joe Neville  I just thought it was striking.
Mr. Tomás Campbell  I am not sure I can comment on the Department of public expenditure's-----
Deputy Joe Neville  I will not say the name but it was striking.

Mr. Tomás Campbell  As I mentioned, we in the Department have been very concerned about this project all along. When you look at the Arts Council IT project, the failings outlined in this committee's report or the Niamh Brennan report were around not having formal structures in place and not escalating these issues up the line. We have those with the MPGOG. We have our independent members.

Deputy Joe Neville  My fear here is that it was up the line. My fear is that it was at very senior levels. We have been told that it was at very senior levels yet no decision was made until somebody else came in when somebody left. Then someone else sits here and deals with the consequences. What we see in here all too often is somebody new like Ms Considine having to answer questions about something that happened prior to her tenure. She is having to answer the questions but all those flags were there along the way. There was a significant failure somewhere. I am not saying it was with the Department of Transport but something definitely happened. Money was being spent and wasted and the flags were there, but everyone was tipping along. Then they were out the door and we are left dealing with a mess here. All too often we have seen the same trend.

Mr. Tomás Campbell  What really changed in the last few months was that Indra delivered the software for CP1 in April. That was the point at which the impairment decision was made and decisions were made about the future of the project and getting onto a sustainable footing going forward.
Deputy Joe Neville  I am going to ask about the timeline. Mr. Campbell has just spoken about April. When did Ms Considine say she came in? Was it nine months ago?
Ms Mary Considine  I took over in October.
Deputy Joe Neville  When was her first board meeting?
Ms Mary Considine  At the end of October.

Deputy Joe Neville  She knew on 1 October. We are talking about April. Even if she was not told at her first one, I am sure it was not the first time it was raised at board level. For the Department of public expenditure to say the first indication it had was in April is significant in itself.
Mr. Tomás Campbell  Just to clarify for the Deputy, I am from the Department of Transport.
Deputy Joe Neville  Well, the Department of Transport or the Department of public expenditure.

Mr. Tomás Campbell  We knew we had serious concerns about the programme for the past four years. We had a number of deep dives on the project as well. We were concerned about the management of the project itself. We were assured by NTA and Iarnród Éireann management but also we were concerned about the wider portfolio of rail projects and what mitigants were in place. For the Waterford North Quays, Galway Ceannt and Foynes line projects, mitigants were in place. I have mentioned the infrastructure management of the annual contract, which is a mitigant for the greater Dublin area. We have a concern about Cork as well. Ms Considine has mentioned that we are working that through to ensure we can bring Cork online. We have been aware of the issues with this project all along and we have had a number of deep dive discussions on it. We have been escalating that to the Minister and to senior management in the Department as well.

Deputy Séamus McGrath  I thank all the witnesses for staying for so long with us to take some supplementary questions. The more I hear, the more I realise the €50 million figure is going to grow significantly. It is not €50 million but a lot more due to the flawed decision to proceed with this project and sign the contract with Indra back in 2020. Just to clarify, the €50 million write-down is one thing and the report that has been commissioned by the NTA is an extra €230,000. The €3 million expenditure in the year to date is effectively part of the written-off project.
Ms Mary Considine  It is written off, yes.

Deputy Séamus McGrath  That is in addition to the €50 million. Some of that was to Indra and some to third parties. The Chair was probing this, but on the interim works that were required to keep the traffic management system safe and up to speed - works that would not have been necessary if a project was delivered in 2024, for example - what is the amount from 2024 up to now? What was spent between 2020 and 2024 was necessary in any event but between 2024, when the new system should have been in place, and now how much has been spent keeping alive the system that is there?

Ms Mary Considine  I do not have that figure. I imagine a lot of that work was done by our team in the signalling electrical area, as part of the infrastructure management. That would be part of their day job of supporting the existing system and keeping it going.
Deputy Séamus McGrath  But it took resources and it was necessary because the new system was not delivered in 2024. The point is that it is an aggregate cost in terms of the overall waste.
Ms Mary Considine  To clarify in case there is any confusion, we have been keeping the system we have, which is life-expired, going. That is done by our own team and they are supporting it-----
Deputy Séamus McGrath  I understand.
Ms Mary Considine  -----with their spare parts and all that and the experience they have in managing it. I think the Deputy is asking what we have spent on maintaining an old system. Separately-----
Deputy Séamus McGrath  From 2024 until now. In 2024 we should have had a new system but we did not. Obviously the old system had to be kept going and that cost extra money.

Ms Mary Considine  Yes, and I do not know how much. I do not think it would have been very significant but we will come back. I do not know that figure. We are looking at ways forward to derisk the train control.
Deputy Séamus McGrath  I know. The €50 million is what is quoted repeatedly but it is much more than that, ultimately. There will be ongoing legal actions. That is confirmed.
Ms Mary Considine  It is not confirmed but we are obviously looking at all legal considerations at the moment in relation to the contract.
Deputy Séamus McGrath  It is highly likely there will be ongoing legal actions, which is an additional cost. Going back to the original tender, what was the original contract value with Indra?
Mr. Paul Hendrick  The target price was €16.4 million, excluding VAT.
Deputy Séamus McGrath  That was the contract value.
Mr. Paul Hendrick  That was the build contract. There was a different price for the maintenance. If it got it built, there was an annual price to manage that system going forward, but the-----
Deputy Séamus McGrath  Just help me to understand that. We have a €50 million write-down but the original contract was €16 million. Just explain that to me.

Mr. Paul Hendrick  In the write-down, the equivalent of the €16 million including VAT was circa €20 million.  Through the commercial resetting we did under resets 1 and 2, that has brought that contract up to about €30 million. We have written down about €28 million of that €30 million because it was predominantly, as we talked about earlier in response to Deputy Neville, the software and part of the hardware. The other costs between the €30 million and the €50 million are also the level of effort we expended with some of our support organisations and our own staff. We went through every single resource. Every effort was allocated to supporting Indra on the software. Once you write down the software, the other writedowns happen as a function of that. It is an indirect consequence of it. That is what brings us up to the €50 million. It is the Indra contract price.
Deputy Séamus McGrath  The original contract was €16 million. The writedown was €50 million because of all those actions that had to be taken. Is that correct?

Mr. Paul Hendrick  It is carrying writedown on other contracts, not just Indra, if that makes sense. There is the Indra contract and the writedown of that. The corollary of that is that in respect of any of the other contracts that were supporting the particular element that has failed, which is the software, we had to make an assessment based on what those individuals were doing in every given month throughout the contract period to identify whether it was linked to that or not in order to comply with our duties regarding the financial statements. That is how we got to that figure.

Ms Mary Considine  If I may add, the €50 million includes VAT. It would be €43 million plus €7 million in VAT. The €7 million, obviously, goes back to the Exchequer. All our figures and schedules include VAT because we do not recover VAT.

Deputy Séamus McGrath  To return to my original train of thought, we are at €54 million in terms of the report commissioned, the €3 million this year, the €50 million and the interim works that had to be done on the system. We do not have a figure on that, but I presume it is adding up to a few hundred thousand. I am speculating on that. We now also have to deliver a new system. We are six years on. We have inflation, which, it could be argued, will add 30% or 40% to what the value should have been. It is potentially tens of millions in additional costs in that. The €50 million is only the baseline really.
Ms Mary Considine  The Deputy is correct. There will be additional costs, unfortunately, but we need a train control system and-----
Deputy Séamus McGrath  I understand that.
Ms Mary Considine  -----and we need to move forward.
Deputy Séamus McGrath  I am just saying that quantifying this broad decision at €50 million is not accurate. It is much more than €50 million.
Ms Mary Considine  Yes. The sum of €50 million is just the impairment.
Deputy Séamus McGrath  We cannot settle on a figure, but it is clearly going to be tens of millions more than €50 million.

Mr. Paul Hendrick  On the impairment figure for the financial statement, we still carry the full cost of the project as €153 million we have spent to date and whatever we have to spend on top of that. We do not lose that number from how we report the project, but the point is well made.

Deputy Séamus McGrath  I will move on briefly to the NTA, if I may, in relation to a local issue. There are ongoing reliability issues with the bus service in Cork. They have been going on for years. There is deep frustration among the public regarding the cancellation of buses, ongoing unreliability, late buses and the information app not providing accurate information over the years. Endless representations have been made. We have been told that the recruitment of drivers will solve the problem, that new buses are being delivered and that investment is being made, yet we continue to have reliability issues. Is there any end to this?

Ms Anne Shaw  There is continued investment in the bus network in Cork. There were issues with driver recruitment, but I am pleased to say Bus Éireann is now fully staffed in terms of the numbers of drivers they need for the services they are running. We had intended this year to begin the first phase of the BusConnects service redesign this year. We are still in discussions with the Department of Transport to make sure that we do that next year. We have already put those bus stops in place and they are ready for those new services. There has been some investment down there as well. We are also investing in electrification and Tivoli depot, which I mentioned in my opening statement, is due to open in the next month. That will enable the buses to go out of the current depot to be sited over there. The current depot can then be taken over in terms of putting in the required electrification and so on. It can then also receive some of those electric buses.  There are also issues with bus reliability, as the Deputy mentioned. Older buses are running at the moment. The intention of the electrification programme is to replace those buses. Bus Éireann has also recruited additional mechanics, etc., to get those back on the ground. The current depot is very constrained in terms of being able to do the mechanical repairs, fix the engines, etc. The temporary depot in Tivoli will enable more maintenance to be carried out. It will address some of the issues of buses being off the road.
Deputy James Geoghegan  I thank the witnesses for staying on. Was the NTA aware that Indra's original bid was 50% lower in pricing terms?
Mr. Hugh Creegan  I am not sure we got the full details. We were certainly informed and gave our consent to award the contract back in 2019.
Deputy James Geoghegan  Did the NTA have sight of its abnormally low price in the investigation that took place?

Mr. Hugh Creegan  Usually we would and we would usually be informed that the valuation has taken place, that an assessment has concluded and that a certain amount has been recommended, seeking our approval. That would usually be the case. I cannot say for certain. I have not looked back-----
Deputy James Geoghegan  In Mr. Creegan's long experience, has he seen such a big variance in price, 50%, for a contract as big as this?

Mr. Hugh Creegan  When it comes to systems being bought and something that may be available, there can be big differences. One entity may have a product that is very close to the requirements and another entity may have to do a whole lot of work to get it. A total of 50% is large, but I have seen some up at that level.
Deputy James Geoghegan  Can the public accounts committee be furnished with details of the investigation that took place at the time - the abnormally low-bid investigation?
Mr. Hugh Creegan  I am not aware that an abnormally low-bid investigation took place-----
Deputy James Geoghegan  I am sorry; Mr. Hendrick said it did.

Mr. Paul Hendrick  I did not say that. I said we assessed the tenders just to make sure when we look at them that there is not anything in there that looks unusual. The abnormally low tenders legislation or case law came in in the last few years, but we would have always looked at it to make sure that the tender price is right and reflective of the works we need to do.
Deputy James Geoghegan  Irish Rail did not carry out a Regulation No. 69 abnormally low tender investigation.
Mr. Paul Hendrick  I am not saying that. We do a full procurement assessment-----
Deputy James Geoghegan  I am asking the question. Which is it? I thought Mr. Hendrick gave evidence that Irish Rail had carried out a Regulation No. 69 abnormally low bid investigation.

Mr. Paul Hendrick  I would have to come back to the Deputy. I was not in the business at the time. We can come back to the Deputy with the report that we would do in terms of the procurement assessment.
Deputy James Geoghegan  Every contracting authority, when an abnormally low bid comes in, under EU law and therefore Irish law, has a legal obligation to carry out an investigation. Did that happen?

Mr. Paul Hendrick  I would have to come back to the Deputy to confirm that. I would expect that it did in terms of what we have done. All our procurements are compliant and we get audited within the business from all our procurements. Nothing has been identified as an issue in terms of how we did the procurement process-----

Deputy James Geoghegan  Mr. Hendrick might examine that and come back to the committee. If an investigation was, in fact, carried out, he might provide a report. If an investigation was not carried out, he might provide an explanation as to why it was not carried out at that time. I take his point about the laws and their application. All that is relevant is how they were interpreted at that time.
Mr. Paul Hendrick  That is fine. We can do that.

Deputy James Geoghegan  The asset value of the TMS software that is being carried or assessed on Iarnród Éireann's books is €100 million. It was €100 million when the impairment review was carried out.
Ms Mary Considine  It is €100 million for the project. That includes the building, the enabling works, hardware and all that stuff.

Deputy James Geoghegan  I will ask the questions straight. When Indra bid to provide the TMS piece, what value did it put on the project originally? For how much did it say it could deliver TMS project originally?
Ms Mary Considine  As my colleague Mr. Hendrick mentioned earlier on, including VAT, it was around €20 million initially.
Deputy James Geoghegan  What did that balloon to?

Ms Mary Considine  We wrote off €28 million from Indra and then there were third-party costs. There would also have been third-party costs in the project budget, but they have increased significantly because the whole project has been elongated.

Deputy James Geoghegan  Initially, it was going to deliver this project for €20 million. Let us fast-forward miles ahead to March 2026, when the project team presented to the board. Presumably, the project team's presentation to the board was a representation of what Indra was telling the project team. Is that fair? I am going back to the €250 million here now.

Mr. Paul Hendrick  If I could just go back to the Deputy's question on the €20 million contract price, the commercial reset number 2 reset that to €36 million, including VAT. There was also commercial reset number 1, which reset it as well-----
Deputy James Geoghegan  Round 1 was €20 million and round 2 was €36 million.

Mr. Paul Hendrick  The assessment team would have made a determination on its own basis - not necessarily on the basis of a direct engagement with Indra but on its own knowledge of the costs and expenditure on the project at a projection-----
Deputy James Geoghegan  Is Mr. Hendrick on the project team?
Mr. Paul Hendrick  The project team is reporting to me.
Deputy James Geoghegan  Mr. Hendrick presented to the board in March 2026. Is that right?
Mr. Paul Hendrick  It is me and the project team. The project team presents.
Deputy James Geoghegan  It is Mr. Hendrick and the project team. They went to the board.  They told the board their assessment was that the global cost would be €250 million.
Mr. Paul Hendrick  That it could be.
Deputy James Geoghegan  It could be, in the best-case scenario, if we can continue with Indra. Is that right?
Mr. Paul Hendrick  Yes, and that was based on years of continuing on this project.
Deputy James Geoghegan  That was the optimistic assessment. Did Mr. Hendrick have other scenarios? Did he have a worst-case scenario?
Mr. Paul Hendrick  No, we did not.
Deputy James Geoghegan  Mr. Hendrick went to the board with one figure, €250 million. Will he break it down and subtract the building costs from the €250 million? What is the TMS piece?
Mr. Paul Hendrick  I cannot, at this stage, but we can come back to the Deputy on it.
Deputy James Geoghegan  Come on. Mr. Hendrick is the project team manager and he cannot tell me, out of the €250 million, how much of that relates to the software. Does he know that figure right now?
Mr. Paul Hendrick  No, I do not. I can come back to the Deputy on it.
Deputy James Geoghegan  What does Mr. Hendrick think it is? Come on. Mr. Hendrick presented to the board. He is being scrutinised by his board as to what this is. How can he not know?
Mr. Paul Hendrick  We did not present a breakdown.
Deputy James Geoghegan  That was in March and we are now in July.
Mr. Paul Hendrick  We did not present a breakdown, so I will have to come back to the Deputy with the details.
Deputy James Geoghegan  What is the build cost then, currently?

Mr. Paul Hendrick  If we go to the €150 million we have spent to the end of 2025, of that €65 million is against the building asset and €85 million is against all the signalling works we did, including the TMS and the signalling enabling works. That brings us up to €150 million to the end of 2025.
Deputy James Geoghegan  That is €150 million on the build site. Is that correct?
Mr. Paul Hendrick  It is €150 million on signalling and on the building.
Deputy James Geoghegan  It would be €250 million if it was kept running.
Mr. Paul Hendrick  Yes, it is a projection of the €150 million continuing.
Deputy James Geoghegan  Is it 60:40, 50:50 or 80:20? Is Mr. Hendrick honestly saying that he cannot even give me a framing between build and software? They are two separate things.
Mr. Paul Hendrick  Sorry, the build is finished, so it would be predominantly on the signalling and TMS system.
Deputy James Geoghegan  Okay, so what does that figure look like? There is €250 million and that includes the building. What is the TMS figure if it ran all the way?
Mr. Paul Hendrick  It would be €250 million, minus the €67 million for the building.
Deputy James Geoghegan  It is €250 million, minus €67 million. Is that what Mr. Hendrick said?
Mr. Paul Hendrick  Correct, including VAT.
Ms Mary Considine  To clarify, there are also works done on signalling, SET and all that kind of stuff, which all has value. There is still €19 million of value in the signalling.
Deputy James Geoghegan  Roughly speaking, we are talking about €180 million if Iarnród Éireann kept going with Indra on the TMS software, based on what I have just been told.
Mr. Paul Hendrick  For all of the signalling systems, excluding the building but including Indra, yes.
Deputy James Geoghegan  We would be talking about €180 million to the very end, on a project that, in the original tender, the company said would be €20 million.
Mr. Paul Hendrick  Other costs are included in there, so it is not a direct comparison.
Deputy James Geoghegan  They are probably marginal enough, though. Will Mr. Hendrick subtract those costs for me?

Mr. Paul Hendrick  If we could say roughly, the original budget would have had approximately the €65 million for the building, which is good, and €85 million for the rest. If we do it against the €85 million, that would be a more direct comparison in terms of the question the Deputy is asking.
Deputy James Geoghegan  How did Iarnród Éireann start with €20 million, get to €85 million and then get to what looks to me like €140 million to €180 million, if it ran it the whole way?
Mr. Paul Hendrick  It is based on assessment of resources working on the project from Indra-----
Deputy James Geoghegan  How did the project balloon to such an enormous degree, from day one to where we are now?

Mr. Paul Hendrick  The problem with this project, all the way through, comes back to the lack of a developed product from Indra. The prolongation on the project, where it is continuing and the resources that are working on the project continue to support this delayed project, obviously get booked to the project cost. The reason this project is delayed and is delaying us continuing all comes back to the lack of a developed product from Indra. That is the source of all of the issues.
Deputy James Geoghegan  I am over time so I ask for the indulgence of the Chair. Has a termination notice been issued to Indra?
Ms Mary Considine  We are still in contract with Indra. As I said at the outset, we are in a sensitive legal and commercial position, so we are still in contract.
Deputy James Geoghegan  The NTA has approved Iarnród Éireann's request to issue a termination notice. Is that correct?
Ms Mary Considine  It has approved the decision taken by our board. We have not implemented those decisions yet.
Deputy James Geoghegan  Is there no other governance check that has to be gone through to execute on the decision of the board?
Ms Mary Considine  Not from an approval's perspective but we need to look at the legal options.
Deputy James Geoghegan  Iarnród Éireann will not be going back to the NTA or the Department on the next steps. It is all in its world now. Is that correct?
Ms Mary Considine  Yes, it is back to us.

An Cathaoirleach  I have a few concluding questions. I want to go back to the implications of this regarding the cost and the delivery of expanded services. Earlier, Ms Shaw, you said you would have to look at phasing of different schemes in the future. You said there was no impact on the Metro and DART+ projects. I ask you to elaborate. I know there is a process of re-evaluation but what people in Wicklow want to hear is that there will be no impact on the DART+ Coastal South expansion to Wicklow town. What assurances can you give people in my constituency, and others across the State, that are eagerly waiting for expansion of services?

Ms Anne Shaw  Ultimately, we understand that to deliver the public transport system for this country, we need to make sure that we progress all of the projects we have identified in our investment plans. We need to understand what the next steps are. That is what we and Irish Rail will be concentrating on in terms of how we get to the traffic management system. Ms Considine has already explained what measures are being taken to protect the greater Dublin area. That probably answers the question about DART+ Coastal South in Wicklow.
An Cathaoirleach  Expansion to Wicklow is still on track for 2029. Is that correct?
Ms Anne Shaw  The resilience project that Irish Rail will be delivering will ensure that there is no impact on the DART+ service.

An Cathaoirleach  With the process that will be embarked on, when will we know what services will be impacted in terms of further expansion or the real impact it will have on users of the rail network?

Ms Anne Shaw  There is a lot of work to be done to understand what the next steps are, working with Irish Rail on how we deliver the traffic management system for the rest of the country. We need to establish the costs and the delivery method. Once we have certainty on the delivery and the costs, we will also be looking across the wider programme.
An Cathaoirleach  When can we expect to have that?
Ms Anne Shaw  We have to work quite quickly, so over the next few months we should at least have some idea about what the implications are, at least an outline. Detail-----
An Cathaoirleach  I ask you to revert to the committee as soon as you have that.
Ms Anne Shaw  -----will need to come through the business cases that we will take through the usual governance processes as well.
